methodology: Named earned-degree holders found by reviewing each school's notable-alumni material and the relevant official award or office records. Count a person once per school and category. Include all genders and historical school names; exclude honorary-only degrees, attendance without an earned degree, nominees, finalists, team members without an individual award, and executives without the qualifying title and year overlap. These are verified named graduates in the reviewed sources, not a claim of complete all-time coverage.

categories.name: Nobel Prize winners
categories.definition: Named Nobel laureates who earned a DePauw or Wabash degree.

depauw.notes: Reviewed DePauw's 100 CLAS Alumni roster, notable alumni and Nobel laureate records. Ferid Murad is the verified graduate; Nobel laureates listed as lecture guests or unrelated alumni are excluded.

wabash.notes: Reviewed Wabash alumni materials and Nobel laureate records. No Wabash graduate qualifying in the reviewed records; visitors and unrelated Nobel recipients are excluded.

categories.name: U.S. vice presidents
categories.definition: People who served as Vice President of the United States and earned a degree from either school.

depauw.notes: Reviewed DePauw alumni and federal biographies. Dan Quayle graduated in 1969.

wabash.notes: Reviewed Wabash alumni and federal biographies. Thomas R. Marshall graduated in 1873.

categories.name: U.S. senators
categories.definition: People who served in the U.S. Senate; state legislators do not qualify.

depauw.notes: Reviewed the official Congressional Biographical Directory biographies for DePauw graduates and Senate service. The documented graduates are Albert J. Beveridge, James Harlan, Joseph E. McDonald, Newton Booth, James Watson, Elmer Thomas, Daniel Voorhees, and Dan Quayle. State legislators alone are excluded.

sources.label: Official Congressional Biographical Directory, searchable member biographies

wabash.notes: Reviewed Wabash graduate and federal office biographies. Mike Braun, Raymond E. Willis, and John Lockwood Wilson have documented U.S. Senate service. Joseph E. McDonald attended Wabash but graduated from DePauw, so he is counted only for DePauw.

sources.label: Official U.S. Congressional Biographical Directory entries, with individual page links in each record

categories.name: U.S. representatives
categories.definition: People who served in the U.S. House of Representatives; state legislative service does not qualify.

depauw.notes: Reviewed the official Congressional Biographical Directory biographies for DePauw graduates and House service. The directory provides degree and federal House-term evidence for listed members; state or territorial legislative service alone is excluded.

sources.label: Official U.S. Congressional Biographical Directory entries, with individual page links in each record
U.S. House History, Art & Archives biographies

wabash.notes: Reviewed Wabash graduates against the official Congressional Biographical Directory and U.S. House History, Art & Archives biographies for federal House terms. Individual sources document earned degrees and service; state representatives and senators alone are excluded.

sources.label: Official U.S. Congressional Biographical Directory entries, with individual page links in each record
U.S. House History, Art & Archives biographies

categories.name: U.S. state governors
categories.definition: People who served as governor of a U.S. state; territorial governors and lieutenant governors do not qualify.

depauw.notes: Reviewed DePauw graduate records and National Governors Association biographies. Verified degree holders include Henry A. Buchtel, Samuel H. Elrod (1882), Newton Booth, and Albert G. Porter. James P. Goodrich and Andrew H. Burke attended but did not earn degrees; lieutenant governors and territorial governors are excluded.

sources.label: National Park Service historic record for DePauw alumni

wabash.notes: Reviewed Wabash graduates against National Governors Association state governor biographies. Thomas R. Marshall and Mike Braun are included; Richard Ristine is excluded because he was lieutenant governor, not governor.

categories.name: Fortune 500 CEOs
categories.definition: People who served as chief executive officer of a company on the U.S. Fortune 500 during an overlapping ranking year; subsidiaries and chair-only roles do not qualify.

depauw.notes: Reviewed named DePauw business leaders in College records against company leadership biographies and dated U.S. Fortune 500 lists. Each displayed graduate has a sourced CEO tenure and at least one matching Fortune ranking year; chair-only roles are excluded.

wabash.notes: Reviewed named Wabash business leaders against school class records, company biographies, historical U.S. Fortune 500 lists, and the Congressional Research Service 1983 executive directory. Robert E. Allen, W. Paul Tippett, and Walter Y. Elisha have sourced degree evidence, CEO service, and an overlapping rank. James L. Keyes is excluded: he is not the Johnson Controls CEO James H. Keyes.

sources.label: Wabash political science alumni: Robert E. Allen ’57

categories.name: Pulitzer Prize winners
categories.definition: Named individual Pulitzer Prize recipients; nominees, finalists, and contributors to a winning organization without an individual prize are excluded.

depauw.notes: Reviewed the DePauw official alumni roster and Pulitzer recipients. Named DePauw graduate recipients are Barbara Kingsolver, James B. Stewart, and Albert J. Beveridge.

wabash.notes: Reviewed Wabash alumni records against the Pulitzer database. Byron Price (Wabash 1912) received the 1944 Pulitzer special citation for distinguished public service in war reporting. Faculty, visitors, honorary alumni, nominees, and contributors without a named prize are excluded.

sources.label: Indiana Journalism Hall of Fame biography: Byron Price

categories.name: Rhodes Scholars
categories.definition: Named Rhodes Scholarship awardees who earned a degree from either college; finalists do not qualify.

depauw.notes: Reviewed the official Rhodes House award records returned for DePauw and traced earned-degree evidence for the named graduates. Three degree-holders are supported in the reviewed sources: Douglas Hallward-Driemeier (1989), John McNaughton (1948 award; DePauw 1942), and Robert Montgomery Stephenson (1916 award; A.B. 1913). This count does not assert an exhaustive historical roster.

sources.label: Harvard Crimson, 1916 degree list for Robert Stephenson

wabash.notes: Reviewed College records of Rhodes graduates and individual alumni biographies. The College identifies nine graduates through Jacob Burnett '15; Chase Breaux '24 is explicitly a finalist and excluded.

categories.name: Astronauts who flew in space
categories.definition: People who completed at least one spaceflight as a crewed spacecraft astronaut; selection without a flight does not qualify.

depauw.notes: Reviewed DePauw notable alumni material against NASA astronaut records. Joseph P. Allen IV (DePauw 1959) flew on STS-5 and STS-51A; no other qualifying graduate identified in the sources reviewed.

wabash.notes: Reviewed Wabash notable alumni and NASA former astronaut records; no earned-degree Wabash graduate with a completed spaceflight was identified in the reviewed records.

categories.name: Academy Award winners
categories.definition: Named individual competitive Academy Award winners; nominees and people merely affiliated with a winning film are excluded.

depauw.notes: Reviewed DePauw graduate material against the Academy’s 96th Oscars ceremony record. Steven Rales won as a named co-producer of The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar. Film affiliates without an individual award are excluded.

sources.label: DePauw record for Steven Rales, class of 1973

wabash.notes: Reviewed Wabash alumni material against the Academy Awards database. Dean Jagger is excluded because he attended Wabash but did not earn a degree there; film affiliations and nominations alone do not qualify.
